newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares gain 0.9 pct despite profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares gain 0.9 pct despite profit-taking.

text.p: Istanbul shares posted gains in selective activity on Thursday, but fell from early highs on profit-taking as the market mostly disregarded the government's second resource package, brokerage.

The IMKB-100 closed up 622.55 points, or 0.92 percent at 68,296.49, but was down from a morning high of 68,745. Non-stop gains totalled 5.4 percent so far this week after last week's 2.1 percent rise.
Trade volume jumped to 14.43 trillion lira from Wednesday's 10.83 trillion.

"The package could not be fully assessed. Only witholding tax on Treasury bills and bonds affected the t-bill rates briefly. There was already a need for a pull back after the recent sharp gains," said Murat Iman from Ata securities.
"The market's own dynamics are in charge. It is likely to rise again after easing," he added.
Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan presented his government's second revenue-raising package aiming to earn another $10 billion.
It aims to mobilise 11 categories of resources including sale of property owned by troubled social security institutions, declaration of unregistered precious metal stocks.
Also introduced was a 10 witholding tax on interest gains on t-bills and bonds to be issued with 1997 maturity. The tax will not be retroactive.

The market mainly awaits implementation of the package details, but PM Erbakan's words that state Etibank would be the first in sell offs buoyed privatisation hopes and fuelled activity in shares of largely state owned stocks.

Many brokers expect the market to move towards 70,000 mark next week amid positive sentiment due to lower t-bill auction rates, cheap share prices in dollar terms and newly emerging nine-month profit outlooks of companies.
The 85-share industrial index firmed 0.58 percent to 74,715.27 and the 15-share financial index leapt 1.8 percent to 60,925.65. Of the 222 issues traded, 92 advanced, 65 declined and 65 were stable.

Actives were led by utility Aktas Elektrik which gained 3,500 lira to 45,000, largely state-owned flat steel giant Eregli, up 300 lira at 10,000, utility Kepez Elektrik, up 2,000 lira at 74,000 and its associate Cukurova Elektrik, up 1,000 lira at 70,000. -- Aydan Eksin, Istanbul newsroom +90-212-275 0875.
